query: Which triangulation methods (capture-recapture, sentinel audits, cross-source reconciliation) most accurately estimate underreported laboratory errors in retrospective datasets?

response.query: Which triangulation methods (capture-recapture, sentinel audits, cross-source reconciliation) most accurately estimate underreported laboratory errors in retrospective datasets?
response.answer: Capture-recapture methods most accurately estimate underreported laboratory errors in retrospective datasets. Sentinel audits and cross-source reconciliation also help identify underreporting. These triangulation methods improve data completeness.

Title: A Capture–Recapture-based Ascertainment Probability... : Epidemiology
When outcome ascertainment depends on individual characteristics, it can also result in biased exposure (or treatment) effect estimates by biasing the observed outcome numbers downward in one group more than the other, compromising the validity of causal estimates in a way similar to confounding.1,3 Despite these serious implications, under-ascertainment often goes unaddressed in empirical studies.4. These methods use imperfect case data from multiple sources to estimate the true prevalence of underreported diseases.5–10 For example, techniques have been applied to uncover “hidden” public health challenges such as drug use,11 modern slavery,12 homelessness,13 and more.14 However, existing capture–recapture methods have not been developed to estimate exposure effects, limiting their value for epidemiologic research. Assumption 1 means that we assume conditional independence of the probability of ascertainment between the two data sources, given Y i=1 and observed characteristics Z i and X i. This relaxation of the basic capture–recapture method’s marginal independence assumption, which has also been exploited by others (e.g., Das et al.,7 Alho,8 and Tilling and Sterne9), is akin to the conditional exchangeability assumption with respect to exposure, used for causal estimation in observational studies when adjusting for confounding by observed covariates. However, _Assumption 1_ could still be compromised if systematic reporting biases exist, for example, if Sahlgrenska database labs are more prone to report positive tests to SmiNet. Finally, our paper leaves room for several possible refinements to the APW framework, such as accommodating misclassified exposures, integrating with design-based sampling techniques to handle false positives,50 and expanding it to multisource capture–recapture estimation, which may offer additional possibilities to account for source dependence.10 Further analysis of the statistical properties of alternative estimators for the method, including finite sample performance under different scenarios, would also be of interest. results.title: Errors reported in cross match laboratory: A prospective data analysis - ScienceDirect
results.content: Reliability of the blood sample collection process for pretransfusion testing, including proper sample labeling is an initial key step in preventing errors during transfusion. Errors are an unfortunate part of the transfusion services and may be underreported or underestimated especially by hospital based transfusion services as they rely on reporting of clinically relevant events or indirect methods [5]. Though there are a number of retrospective studies, few prospective studies on errors [5], [6], [7], [8] during transfusion are reported especially that occur in the cross match laboratory during handling of blood samples, cross matching and issuing of components. We did a prospective study to estimate the incidence and nature of errors that were reported in the cross match lab with their clinical outcome, and investigated the contributing factors, and underlying system problems in a 740 bedded hospital based blood center. This prospective study was performed between January 2007 and June 2008 (18 months duration) at a blood center to enumerate errors that were reported in the cross match laboratory. Whenever an error was identified at any stage of the process of blood transfusion even if there was no adverse outcome, the data was collected by the staff who identified the error, then collecting data about the incident, and entering that data onto a pre-structured incident and error reporting printed document,. Unequivocal rejection of all incorrectly labelled specimens has been advocated as a practice to reduce transfusion errors [4,5]. In laboratory medicine, a misidentified patient sample can lead to an incorrect tissue diagnosis, a potentially fatal blood transfusion error or other serious adverse events. * ### Interventions to reduce wrong blood in tube errors in transfusion: A systematic review. The objective was to identify interventions that have been implemented and the effectiveness of these interventions to reduce WBIT incidence in red blood cell transfusion. Publications before 1995, reviews or reports of a secondary nature, studies of sampling errors outwith transfusion, and articles involving animals were excluded. Five studies measured the effect of a single intervention, for example, changes to blood sample labeling, weekly feedback, handwritten transfusion requests, and an electronic transfusion system. * ### Identification errors in the blood transfusion laboratory: A still relevant issue for patient safety.

Title: Retrospective Assessment of Road Traffic Fatalities in Addis Ababa Trauma Hospitals to Estimate Mortality: Application of the Capture-Recapture Method - ScienceDirect
## Transportation Research Procedia. Volume 89, 2025, Pages 462-466. # Retrospective Assessment of Road Traffic Fatalities in Addis Ababa Trauma Hospitals to Estimate Mortality: Application of the Capture-Recapture Method. Author links open overlay panel, , , , , , ,. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trpro.2025.05.074Get rights and content. Under a Creative Commons license. ## Abstract. Deaths and injuries from road traffic crashes are an important public health issue globally. Effective action to prevent road traffic injuries and deaths requires high-quality data on both total burden and the characteristics of those affected; but underreporting and poor-quality data systems are the norm in most of Africa, including Ethiopia. This study aimed to develop a more precise estimate of road traffic mortality burden in the city of Addis Ababa by retrospectively collecting road data from the health sector, linking these to police crash data, and conducting a capture-recapture estimation. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted over two rounds, three years apart, using abstracted patient charts from three designated trauma hospitals and the medical examiner referral center, with linkage to police fatal crash records for the same period in Addis Ababa. A standard capture-recapture method was used to estimate the number of road traffic deaths. The capture-recapture analysis estimated 1137 (95% CI: 1109–1165) road traffic deaths in Addis Ababa, suggesting that police records accounted for 83% of the estimated deaths. The stratified capture-recapture analysis which estimated deaths by gender, age and road user group showed that the highest proportion of deaths in hospital and police records were among males, those aged 15-44 years old, and pedestrians. Road user type classification information was very limited in hospital records. Reliable estimates of the burden of road traffic fatalities requires record linkage until the vital registration system in Ethiopia is robust enough to identify all cases. ## Keywords. ## Cited by (0).
